messages:
Eden: FYI -- I gotta step out at 16:00 for a doctor's appt. Priya, you said you might be +10-15m? We need to confirm primary/secondary for the 16:00-20:00 window and a quick escalation matrix for the EU Dedicated maintenance tonight.
Priya: Yep, running ~10m late. I can take primary at 16:15 if that's ok. Jon can stay as secondary until Sasha rotates in at 18:00.
Jon: I can cover secondary through 18:00. If anything fires before then, page me first, then Sasha.
Eden: Okay lock that in. Two quick constraints to highlight: 1) maintenance will hit eu-west qps shapers -> higher 5xx risk for small number of Dedicated tenants, 2) console deploys are frozen during the window.
Priya: Important: for Dedicated customers with SLA >99.9 we escalate faster. If any tenant shows sustained >30% error rate for 5 minutes, follow the Dedicated escalation path (page Sasha and @pagerduty-oncall, then #customer-ops).
incidents-bot: Scheduled maintenance reminder: EU network maintenance at 17:00-18:30 UTC. Affected: routing layer between eu-west-1 and eu-central-1.
Eden: Quick handoff checklist (copy this when you take over):
- Confirm primary/secondary names in the shift doc
- Check 'eu-dedicated' alerts in Console -> Routing -> Errors (filter by model/pool)
- Re-run healthcheck script for affected pools
- If KV cache misses spike, reduce batch window to 50ms
- If sustained customer impact, flip to fallback model variant and notify CS

Use this command to pull recent error rates (run from eng-prod):
```
# get errors per minute for eu-dedicated
./tools/metrics query --cluster eu-west --metric error_rate --window 10m --group tenant_id
```

Jon: Also: paging rules summary for tonight (per-runbook condensed):
- Minor alert (single pod OOM, <5% customer impact): notify secondary, create incident, no exec page.
- Major alert (>=10% of a tenant's requests failing OR cross-tenant regression): page Sasha (oncall-lead) and @pagerduty-oncall immediately.
- Sev1 (production wide outage or sustained latency >2s P95 across regions): call the Incident Commander on phone, page execs (#exec-oncall) after IC confirms impact.

Priya: I added the Dedicated escalation steps to the shift doc and pinned the runbook link: https://redwood.runbooks/internal/oncall/dedicated-escalation
Eden: Thanks. One more: if it's region-specific (eu-west only) and secondary latency matches primary latency spike, we should route traffic to us-east fallback pool per routing policy A. That's a decision Jon can make w/ Sasha approval.
Sasha: Acknowledged. I'll be reachable by phone at +1-555-0199 after 18:00. If you page me for Dedicated escalation, also tag me in #customer-ops and add tenant IDs.
pagerduty-bot: Incident alert simulated: test page to verify paging chain (do not respond) -> sent to @pagerduty-oncall, @sasha, @jon.
Eden: Quick pre-handoff TTL checks: confirm token rotations, make sure no long-running canaries in pipeline, and verify autoscaler targets for eu-dedicated are not in cooldown.
Priya: I'm taking primary at 16:15. I'll run the pre-handoff steps at 16:05 and post a confirmation here.
Jon: I'll keep secondary and monitor error dashboards. If anything approaches the major threshold, I'll page Sasha and then escalate to #customer-ops.
Eden: Perfect. Post-handoff arrival: Priya should post a short status: primary active, secondary verified, healthchecks green. Then Eden will close the thread.
Priya: Primary active at 16:17. Secondary (Jon) verified. Healthchecks: ok. watching console. :white_check_mark:
Eden: Thanks all. Leaving notes in the shift doc re: fallback thresholds. If you hit an ambiguous case, default to paging Sasha early. Better to over-communicate than under. :phone:
